title: CGST Act s. 16 — Eligibility and conditions for taking Input Tax Credit (ITC) (CGST Act s. 16)

content.overview: Section 16 allows input-tax credit to a registered person on goods or services used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business, if the conditions are met. Those conditions include a tax invoice or debit note, receipt of the goods or services, tax actually paid to the Government, and filing of the return. Credit is not available beyond the time limit in the section, and it fails if depreciation is claimed on the tax component or if payment to the supplier is not made within the stated period. Credit is a condition-based right. A tax invoice alone is not enough.

enhancement.definition: Section 16 allows input-tax credit to a registered person on goods or services used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business, if the conditions are met. Those conditions include a tax invoice or debit note, receipt of the goods or services, tax actually paid to the Government, and filing of the return. enhancement.legalPrinciple: Credit is a condition-based right. A tax invoice alone is not enough.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, section 16.
essentialIngredients: Possession of invoice or debit note
Payment to supplier within the statutory period
No depreciation claimed on the tax component
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 16(1) states the entitlement. Section 16(2) states the conditions. Receipt includes receipt by an agent where the section so treats it. If payment is not made within the period stated in the proviso, the credit already taken is added to output tax, with a restoration if payment is later made. Section 16(4) is the time bar, tied to the November date following the financial year or the annual return, as the section enacts. Blocked credit in section 17 is a different limit.
examples: A registered manufacturer holds a tax invoice, has received the goods, and the supplier has paid the tax.
The same invoice is used after the section 16(4) date.
The time bar is the issue.
Depreciation is claimed on the GST component of a capital good.
